title: Revisiting transportation problems under Monge costs with applications to the Discrete Ordered Median Problem: compact optimal dual solutions from the northwest-corner rule (Theorem 2.5)
author: Stefan Nickel, Justo Puerto, Simon Ramoser, and Alberto Torrejon
work: Revisiting transportation problems under Monge costs with applications to the Discrete Ordered Median Problem
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's compact closed-form expressions for optimal dual solutions of the balanced transportation problem under Monge costs, printed as Theorem 2.5 (source0.tex lines 284-289) and delivered with the paper's own complete proof (lines 290-294). The proof is complete and self-contained apart from the northwest-corner algorithm and the two dual-recursion algorithms, which are delivered as retained context. The author runs an induction on the iterations of the forward dual recursion: after checking the first iteration, the induction step observes that a down move leaves the already assigned dual entry unchanged, so the newly assigned u-entry equals the previous one plus the stated increment c_{k j_k} - c_{k-1, j_k}; the u-formula follows. The v-formula is then obtained by substituting the u-formula into the assignment v_j = c_{i_j j} - u_{i_j} made by the algorithm, identifying the running index as i_j = max{k >= 2 : j_k <= j}, and collapsing the resulting difference of two sums into the stated double sum by a telescoping argument. Carrying this out requires reading the greedy northwest-corner recursion as a staircase path, bookkeeping the index sequence j_i, the dual of the transportation LP, strong duality for it, and the telescoping cancellation between c_{i_j j} and the accumulated sums; the closed forms are the paper's headline theoretical contribution, which its introduction states had not appeared in the literature before, and the paper's two exponential MILP reformulations of the DOMP are built directly on them. No qualifying examination poses the derivation of optimal dual solutions of a Monge transportation problem in closed form from the northwest-corner path. That places the unit in the upper qualifying-to-research range: H2.
